new_statements.rule_in_words: Aimol is described as a tone language with two lexical tones, falling (unmarked) and level (marked), contrasting in minimal pairs (e.g. in 'to drink' vs in 'house', thi 'to die' vs thi 'blood', lun 'heart' vs lun 'stone'). The 85-page phonology chapter, the symbols list and the introduction never mention stress or accent, so no placement rule for word stress exists in this source; the only prominence remark is that falling diphthongs have a louder first element (p. 37).
new_statements.exceptions: None; no stress rule is given at all.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone is stated on monosyllabic citation forms (minimal pairs); syllable section (pp. 94-97) lists V, VC, CV, CVC, CCV, CCVC patterns and words up to seven syllables without any prominence marking. Data from nine informants of the Aimol villages near Pallel Bazar, Chandel district (Sutpong-area varieties), collected c. 1990-95.
new_statements.identity_note: Singh 1995 describes the Aimol of the nine villages 4 km east of Pallel Bazar, Chandel district, Manipur (the valley/Sutpong-area community), with nine named informants; no dialect label is used. Glottolog has a single languoid aimo1244 (no dialect children), so the description maps to the language-level entry. Wikipedia (citing Haokip 2011) distinguishes Sutpong and Khurai dialects; the thesis does not address this split.

sources.note: Nothing about stress or accent anywhere in the prelims, ch. I or ch. II (0 hits for 'stress'/'accent'); p. 14: 26 phonemes incl. '2 (two) suprasegmental phonemes... The suprasegmental phonemes are tones'; sec. 2.5 Tone p. 93: two tones, falling (unmarked) and level (marked), shown by minimal pairs; sec. 2.6 Syllables pp. 94-97 gives V/VC/CV/CVC/CCV/CCVC patterns and mono- to heptasyllabic words with no prominence marking; p. 37 only says falling diphthongs have a louder first element. Ch. I p. 1: 'Aimol is a tone language, and a subject-object-verb language.'

'Tone is an important feature of the language, as the certain pitch used can indicate multiple different words' — uncited; no stress statement; cites Okhup Aimol dictionary for vowels and a now-404 SPPEL page for syllable structure.
